new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Board reports ABSENT: no commodity and no capture match. Not already priced under another spelling - the meat ids in play are ground-beef-8020 and cube/steak cuts; an eye of round is a whole-muscle roasting joint sold by the piece at roast prices, not a ground or steak SKU. No word-order variant (round roast / eye round) appears on the everyday board or the feed.

Priced separately from `mushrooms` (vocabulary label: White Mushrooms) and from `portobello-mushrooms` (large caps sold 2-count). Baby bella/cremini is its own 8 oz tray SKU at a premium to white button - the same variety-pricing call the estate already makes for red onion vs onions. If the registrar judges the premium immaterial, aliasing to `mushrooms` is the acceptable fallback.

registrar_rulings.reason: No round-primal beef id exists anywhere in the estate: re-swept all three namespaces and the live feed for round/rump/london/eye and found only ground-beef variants, ribeye-steak, chuck-roast/beef-chuck-roast, beef-short-ribs and 'birds eye' frozen-vegetable brand hits - no eye-of-round, bottom/top round, rump roast or london broil under any spelling, and no feed price cell. Chuck-roast ($6.64/lb, Sam's) is the nearest live row but is a different purchase, not a variant: chuck is a marbled shoulder braising cut, eye of round a lean whole-muscle roasting joint from the round primal, sold as distinct SKUs at distinct price bands. FOLLOW-UP EDITS: mint in the recipe namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json, since beef roasts go on sale) via the sanctioned editors; include patterns 'eye\s+of\s+round' / 'eye\s+round\s+roast' survive contiguously in real product names; excludes MUST cover 'steak' (eye-of-round STEAK is a thin-cut different purchase), 'ground', 'deli', 'sliced', 'roast beef' lunchmeat, 'jerky', 'pet|dog', 'seasoning', 'gravy', 'broth' - build to the ~150-pattern rigor of a neighboring meat row, not the V4 2-5. Add allowlist pair eye-of-round-roast <-> chuck-roast (reason: different beef primal, different cut) so the shared 'roast' token never pages the daily audit. VOCABULARY: 'Boneless Eye of Round Roast' also needs a new ingredients.json row (no core-word match found) - a separate act; this ruling mints only the id. Macros: fdc:170229 is the COOKED/roasted SR row - use the raw separable-lean-and-fat counterpart or transcribe a label; do not attach cooked macros to a purchase id.

The food is already priced by design: the weekly `mushrooms` row is labeled 'Mushrooms (white / baby bella)' and its include list explicitly claims 'cremini' and 'baby\s*bella' (verified at commodities.json:9467-9474), live at $0.1612/oz across 7 stores - so every cremini tray on shelf is ALREADY captured by this id, and minting cremini-mushrooms would put the same tray under two ids, the exact bread-crumbs defect. The mapper's red-onion analogy fails on the estate's own record: red onion was split BEFORE the base row claimed it, whereas here the pooling of white+cremini is a deliberate, labeled decision, and the recipe-side white-mushrooms row excludes cremini precisely because the weekly pooled row carries it (white-mushrooms -> mushrooms is already a verified floor-map pair). The current crown happens to be a white 8oz tray (Aldi Monterey white sliced, $1.29), so a cremini premium is real but is absorbed by the pool by design; if Brad wants the premium priced separately, that is a REPARTITION of `mushrooms` (remove cremini/baby-bella from its includes, relabel, then mint) - a Brad-level edit, not something this gate may do as a side effect of a new id. FOLLOW-UP EDITS: add recipe-floor-id-map.json pair cremini-mushrooms -> mushrooms (units match, oz/oz); resolve the ingredient name to the existing vocabulary neighbors rather than minting a new row only if Brad rules the variety immaterial for macros - white and cremini macros differ trivially, so reuse is defensible there too.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 486 cal / 10 carbs / 40 protein per serving over 8 servings. Recomputed from the rows above at source scale: about 436 cal and 47 g protein per serving (roast 1474 g raw at 23.5 P/100 g contributes 43 g of that protein; butter 101 cal and olive oil 30 cal carry most of the fat). Protein is +17% against the source and calories -10%. Taking the low end of the stated 3 to 3 1/2 lb range (1361 g) lands protein at exactly 40 g, so the whole gap is the range midpoint I chose plus the source likely costing a fattier grade. Within tolerance, no line re-examined. Carbs recompute to about 8 g against the published 10 - comfortably inside the 35 g cap.
